Around 27 June 2022 (as reported), Ansaru militants beat up a commercial motorcyclist who lives in Unguwar Makera, Kazange ward, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) because he was seen with a sticker of a political aspirant.

On 27 June 2022, soldiers attached to the Forcados terminal shot and killed a civilian in Ogulagha community, coded to Forcados (Burutu, Delta). The victim was a snail hunter who went out in the company of 5 others to pick snails; they were intercepted by soldiers on the way back, the victim tried to flee and he was shot.

On 27 June 2022, soldiers dressed in plain clothes shot sporadically when they clashed with policemen at Edepie-Etegwe roundabout Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The soldiers were driving against traffic and were advised to take the proper lane by the policemen, which resulted in the clash; two persons were hit and wounded by stray bullets.
On 27 June 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians at Ayere (Ijumu, Kogi). The victims were from Ikaram Akoko. A ransom of 40 million naira was demanded.

On 27 June 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Udoda (Ahoada West, Rivers) and killed an unspecified number of person, coded as 3. The assailants broke doors and stole money worth 30 million naira and have killed over 30 people since 2019 [coded separately], according to the Paramount Ruler of the community.

On 27 June 2022, an operative of Amotekun shot and killed a student of Rufus Giwa Polytechnic Owo (Owo, Ondo) in front his parent's residence. The reason for the attack is unknown, the victim died from gunshot wounds ten days later.
On 28 June 2022, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed around the University of Port Harcourt, Choba (Obio, Rivers). An unspecified number of persons were killed, coded as 3.
On 28 June 2022, an unidentified armed group killed five soldiers in villages neighboring Wase (Wase, Plateau).

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF ambushed suspected Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] in the axis of Gubio LGA (Borno). Three militants were killed, one bow and arrow, two rifles and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 28 June 2022, Fulani and Gbagyi ethnic militias clashed in Paikon Kore (Gwagwalada, FCT) following a disagreement over land for planting of pasture and food for consumption, many locals were wounded. Soldiers calmed the situation while policemen fired shots in the air.

Around 28 June 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed the immediate past secretary of Birnin Gwari local council whom they abducted together with and his younger brother from their farm [coded separately]. Location coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), the secretary was murdered after an undisclosed amount had been paid as ransom, while his brother escaped.

On 28 June 2022, Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] ambushed Nigerian troops after detonating an IED on the troops carrying out clearance operation along Miromti and Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed the Civilian JTF commander who attempted to repel their attack in Sabon Gero (Chikun, Kaduna). One resident was also killed, 17 residents including a medical doctor were abducted while six of the abductees escaped. The abductees were released on 13 August, the leader of the Civilian JTF claimed there was no ransom payment.

On 28 June 2022, a Zamfara militia abducted the wife of the chairman of the Zamfara state chapter of NULGE from their residence at Damba in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia was in search of the chairman who hid himself, and his wife pregnant wife was taken. The abductee gave birth in captivity, a ransom of 15 million was paid for the baby and mother's release.

On 28 June 2022, an unidentified armed group comprised of 5 masked men shot and killed a police officer who was returning home from work in Oboama community, Oyigbo (Oyigbo, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian soldiers from the navy and army killed scores of civilians when they invaded Ossomala, Umunankwo and Obeagwa communities, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra) as claimed by residents of the community. The soldiers were reported to be in search of unidentified armed group members, they destroyed traditional sanctuaries and claimed they were linked to IPOB activities. Scores of fatalities split across two events, coded as 10.

On 28 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in large numbers and a large convoy of vehicles attacked civilians in Lassa (Askira Uba, Borno). The militants shot sporadically and broke into stores, they invaded the village after coming from an area near Sambisa forest by Maikadiri and Utavu. Casualties unknown.

On 28 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in their large numbers clashed with Nigerian troops stationed at Maikadiri (Askira Uba, Borno) before they proceeded to attack Lassa town [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.

On 28 June 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an attack by ISWAP militants on a troop's base in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The militants withdrew and fled through Dogsa. Casualties are unknown, ISWAP claimed to have fired three mortar at the barracks.

On 29 June 2022, members of the Enugu state vigilante group shot a 15 year old boy and killed him at his residence for resisting arrest in Nkpologwu community, coded to Umulokpa (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victim was confirmed dead the following day as a result of the injury from the shooting.

Around 29 June 2022 (as reported), soldiers in collaboration with members of a local self defense militia killed a member of an unidentified armed group at Kan Duniya, coded to Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau).

On 29 June 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted an unspecified number of persons from Gadar Zaima, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) on the village market day. The abductees include the village head, a political secretary of a political party from Kyaram ward, a local hunter and many visitors at the market.

Around 29 June 2022 (as reported), one of the abductees from the Kaduna train attack [coded separately] was shot by their abductors during a friendly exchange of fire between the abductors, as claimed by the negotiator who said the victim was in critical condition. Location coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna).

On 29 June 2022, Nigerian soldiers from the navy and army killed scores of civilians when they invaded Ossomala, Umunankwo and Obeagwa communities, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra) as claimed by residents of the community. The soldiers were reported to be in search of unidentified armed group members they destroyed traditional sanctuaries and claimed they were linked to IPOB activities. Scores of fatalities split across two events, coded as 10.

On 29 June 2022, a Niger militia clashed with policemen and ambushed soldiers providing reinforcement when they attacked a mining site at Ajata-Aboki, near Galapai (Shiroro, Niger). 35 soldiers, 7 mobile policemen, and 6 civilians were killed, several persons were wounded, between 2 and 4 Chinese nationals and other workers were abducted. Seven Chinese abductees were rescued by troops of the Nigerian Air Force on 17 December.

On 29 June 2022, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed and two people were killed in two separate attacks in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Other source report that 8 people were killed across Benin City as a result of a clash which was caused by one cult member who abandoned his group and joined a rival cult group.
On 29 June 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian troops at Mairami (Konduga, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 30 June 2022, about 300 members of a Zamfara communal militia including women dressed in military uniforms on motorcycles attacked civilians in Gadar Zaima, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). Two persons were killed and 12 others were abducted.

On 30 June 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with policemen who were on stop and search duty at a checkpoint in Gariki (Enugu South, Enugu). Two policemen were killed, other sources report that an unspecified number of persons were also killed.
On 30 June 2022, policemen raided a camp of IPOB militants and engaged in an armed clash at Oriuzor (Ezza North, Ebonyi). One militant was killed, six others fled with fled with bullet wounds.
On 30 June 2022, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians, killed 20 people and abducted 25 women when they invaded three villages in Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 30 June 2022, a suspected Fulani militia dressed in military and police uniforms attacked civilians and killed two people in Mgbuji and Agu-Amede communities (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Two other persons were wounded.

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP fighters on 5 gun trucks attacked a camp of Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Gazuwa village, coded to near by Bama LGA (Borno). 18 ISWAP and 3 Boko Haram fighters were killed, three out of the five gun trucks were seized by the Boko Haram fighters, the other ISWAP fighters fled on motorcycles and two gun trucks.
On 30 June 2022, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers on a patrol around Amdami forest, Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). Seven soldiers were killed.

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked civilians at Nchiha village in Korongilum ward (Chibok, Borno). Eight villagers including five members of the same family were killed, two other villagers drowned in a river while attempting to escape (total of 10 fatalities).

On 30 June 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired anti-aircraft rifles GPMG at an MNJTF helicopter in Borno, coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The pilot and co-pilot of landed the aircraft successfully and were unhurt.

On 1 May 2022, Nigerian troops of Operation Whirl Stroke clashed with armed individuals at a forest in Sengev council ward, Guma LGA (Benue), coded to Gbajimba, while responding to a distress call. A couple who were abducted by the armed individuals were rescued after the assailants fled and left them behind. No fatalities.

Around 1 May 2022 (as reported), armed individuals on motorcycles killed over 40 persons, including policemen and soldiers, providing protection to a community in the southern part of Taraba state during the Sallah break, as claimed by the Senator representing the Taraba south senatorial district. Location coded to the southern town of Gembu (Sardauna, Taraba).

Around 1 May 2022 (as reported), suspected members of Aiye cult militia, also called Black Axe, killed one person in Ilaro (Egbado South, Ogun). The reason for the attack is unknown, the police claimed to have arrested four militiamen in connection with the attack.

On 1 May 2022, an unidentified rival cult militia clashed with another unidentified cult militia around Okesuna/ Oja Gboro area (Ilorin East, Kwara). One person, suspected to be a member of one of the militias, was killed.

On 1 May 2022, Awawa Boys members attacked residents and killed one person in Shaiba (Agege, Lagos). Residents were robbed of valuables and an unspecified number of others were wounded; the killed victim was attacked with what appeared like cutlasses and sticks.
On 1 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a pastor from his church in the Ajebandele area of Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). There are no report of ransom demands.
On 1 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a lecturer in Oturkpo (Otukpo, Benue), while three other persons escaped being abducted during the event. The abductee escaped from his abductors on 2 May.
On 2 May 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed a farmer on his cashew farm at Araromi village in Igbo Ora (Ibarapa Central, Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, joint task force operatives, presumed to comprise of soldiers, policemen and local defense militiamen, clashed with members of a Niger communal militia around Uregi and Kiribo villages (Rafi, Niger) while the group was attacking civilians. Ten assailants were killed, 14 abductees were rescued, seven motorcycles and arms were recovered.
On 2 May 2022, armed individuals killed two people, including a presumed off duty policeman, beside St Mary's Church in Ozubulu (Ekwusigwo, Anambra). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, armed individuals killed two brothers at Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra). One of the victims, who was a former youth leader, was killed in front of their residence, while the second was blind-folded and abducted by the assailants and later killed close to Utu junction; his corpse was dumped at the center of the road. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 May 2022, Nigerian troops in collaboration with the Civilian JTF, while on a clearance operation, clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in Kayamla village (Konduga, Borno). The militants were on a mission to rustle cattle from pastoralists; three of them were killed and one suspected female collaborator was arrested near the village.

On 2 May 2022, armed individuals suspected to be enforcing a sit in order attacked and beat up a shop owner for opening his shop in Uli (Ihiala, Anambra). The victim's generator set was set ablaze by the assailants.

On 3 May 2022, Yansakai militiamen from Tungar Bido village attacked residents with cutlasses, knives and other weapons and killed one person in Tungar Dutsi village of Gana district (Bukkuyum, Zamfara), coded to Bukuyum. The assailants invaded the village, claimed they were celebrating Sallah and shot sporadically; they attacked residents after they were cautioned against shooting. The leader of the group was arrested by the police, others fled.
On 3 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals abducted the three delegates of the PDP election committee near Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu) while they were enroute to Ebonyi.
On 3 May 2022, ISWAP fighters clashed with Nigerian troops at a forward operation base in Kada, 2 km from Kautakari (Chibok, Borno), dislodging the troops. who fled to Chibok town.

On 3 May 2022, ISWAP fighters attacked civilians in Kautakari (Chibok, Borno). Between 7 to 9 locals were killed; the group looted and set shops and houses ablaze. Hundreds of locals fled into the bush and many others were missing.

On 3 May 2022, suspected IPOB militants attacked policemen at a checkpoint in Obudi-Agwa (Oguta, Imo). One policemen was killed and between one and two others were injured; the assailants cut off the privates part of the killed officer and left with it. The police claimed to have clashed with the assailants at the spot immediately after and killed two armed men while the others escaped. 3 total fatalities.
On 4 May 2022, armed individuals abducted two passengers of a commercial vehicle along the Emohua-Kalabari axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 May 2022, Nigerian troops clashed and killed scores of ISWAP/ Boko Haram and cleared out 24 of their camps in the Bama LGA (Borno) axis. Adamu Ngulde, a commander of the militants, was one of the fatalities, dozens of militants surrendered and more than 900 women and children were rescued. Fatalities coded as 20.
On 4 May 2022, ISWAP militants traced and killed three of their members who were enroute to surrender to Nigerian troops close to Karetu (Mobbar, Borno).

On 4 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with soldiers at Uratta (Aba South, Abia) while they were spreading information about a sit in order slated for the next day. Four armed individuals, including the leader of the group, were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds; some charms and a live tortoise were recovered from the suspected leader.

On 5 May 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed a Fulani man, his wife and son while they were returning from Nguma (Biu, Borno) after some of their members were killed by an IED planted by the group itself [coded separately].
Around 5 May 2022 (as reported), members of a Sokoto militia abducted three residents from Takakume village (Goronyo, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 May 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked residents of Cinke and Zarama villages in Kwal (Bassa, Plateau) and killed eight persons. Two other persons were wounded; several goods were destroyed and stolen.

On 6 May 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with a large number of members of a Zamfara militia when the militia men attacked civilians in Damri (Bakura, Zamfara). Four persons, including one policeman, a NSCDC operative and patients receiving treatment in a hospital were killed; one vehicle belonging to the police was set ablaze. The attack might be related to the clash the group had with the military in the region which killed 10 militiamen two weeks prior (coded separately).

On 6 May 2022, armed individuals enforcing a sit in order shot sporadically at residents when they attacked Ebebe junction of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One vehicle and a motorcycle were set ablaze by the assailants, there were no casualties. The sit in order was in response to President Buhari's visit to the state, IPOB has denied imposing the sit in order.

On 6 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Sabon Gari Damri and Kalahe in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). Between 40 to 56 bodies were recovered. The attack might be related to the clash the group had with the military in the region which killed 10 militiamen two weeks prior (coded separately).
On 6 May 2022, armed individuals suspected to be assassins shot and killed a photographer at his wife's store on Otomewo road in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 7 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked residents and shot sporadically in Faru, Faru Magami ward, location coded to known village on the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). One person was killed in Faru Magami, an unspecified number of persons are missing.

On 7 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals abducted a man at the Okada axis, in or around Okada (Ovia North East, Edo). The abductee was in the company of his son who he was taking to write JAMB examinations, the son was left behind by the abductors.

On 7 May 2022, military forces with local defense militiamen repelled an attack by gunmen in Gurbin Magarya, Jibia LGA (Katsina). Three residents were killed, three others were wounded and livestock belonging to residents were killed by the assailants before the arrival of security operatives.

On 7 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked residents and shot sporadically in Garin Minane village in Maradun LGA (Zamfara). Six persons, four of whom were returning from a farm were killed; an unspecified number of persons are missing.

On 8 May 2022, armed individuals abducted a catholic priest from the premises of his parish in Ikot Abasi Akpan, Mkpat Enin LGA (Akwa Ibom). The assailants invaded the area on a motorcycle and shot sporadically into the air to scare residents away. The abductee was released on 12 May, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 8 May 2022, members of a Sokoto militia clashed with members of a local defense militia as they attacked Takakume (Goronyo, Sokoto). The leader of the assailants was killed by the defense militia. One resident was killed and six others were abducted and later killed by the assailants as revenge for the killing of their leader. Fatalities coded as 8.

On 8 May 2022, armed individuals attacked a truck being driven by assumed Fulani, wounded the driver and set the truck ablaze on the Ezinifitte/ Uga road (Aguata, Anambra). The truck was conveying cattle to a market in the state. One person was rescued and 34 livestock were recovered by the police.

On 9 May 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed three persons in Num area of Sara village, coded to Tafawa-Balewa (Tafawa Balewa, Bauchi). Five persons were wounded by the assailants. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Gini (Muya, Niger), Dandaudu and Gidan Mangoro [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Gini; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 0.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Dandaudu (Muya, Niger), Gini and Gidan Mangoro [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Dandaudu; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 1.

On 9 May 2022, members of a Niger militia killed a Fulani pastoralist when they attacked the villages of Gidan Mangoro (Muya, Niger), Dandaudu and Gini [coded separately]. A person was abducted in Gidan Mangoro; residents fled the area. Fatalities split into 3 events and coded as 0.

On 9 May 2022, a Joint Task Force presumed to comprise of the military, police and local defense militiamen repelled an attack by militants in Jellako community, coded to Kagara (Rafi, Niger). 15 abductees who were abducted from different locations were rescued, two motorcycles were abandoned by the assailants who fled with gunshot wounds.

On 9 May 2022, an armed group numbering up to 20 stabbed and wounded one resident and abducted 3 persons, including the deputy paramount ruler of Otuabula community (Ogbia, Bayelsa). The wounded victim escaped being abducted; there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 9 May 2022, Boko Haram/ISWAP militants killed a Boko Haram commander (who had paid allegiance to ISWAP) at Galta in Madagali LGA (Adamawa) after he was tried and found guilty of 'treasonable felony' over his plans to surrender to the Nigerian troops.
On 9 May 2022, a Katsina communal militia killed one person and stole valuables from Mai Gora (Faskari, Katsina).

On 10 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with Nigerian troops at Ananum village (Donga, Taraba). Two armed persons were killed, others fled with gunshot wounds; weapons, ammunition charms and some money were recovered by the troops.
On 10 May 2022, armed individuals clashed with soldiers after ambushing them in Mararraba (Donga, Taraba). The troops fought off the ambush; two armed men were killed and other were injured.

On 10 May 2022, suspected members of an unidentified cult militia attacked and killed three persons in Inen community, coded to Ikot Ibritam (Oruk Anam, Akwa Ibom). One motorcycle and a POS machine were stolen from the victims by the assailants whom other sources report came from neighboring communities.

On 10 May 2022, suspected sea pirates abducted seven passengers around the Yellow Channel axis between Bonny and Port Harcourt (Bonny, Rivers). The victims were rescued by the Nigerian Navy around 24 May and the Navy claimed no ransom was paid for the release.

On 10 May 2022, gunmen abducted three persons from Maji community (Suleja, Niger). The victims include one nursing mother, a teenage boy and another woman; a ransom of 5 million naira each has been demanded by the abductors.

On 10 May 2022, armed individuals suspected Fulani Ethnic militiamen ambushed the convoy of a commanding officer and clashed with soldiers and mobile police officers at Tati village in Takum LGA (Taraba). 7 security operatives were killed. The commanding officer and his orderly are missing. The police claimed the soldiers were caught in the clash between the Fulani and Kuteb militias.
On 10 May 2022, armed individuals attacked civilians and killed four persons in Ayilamo community (Logo, Benue). Several others persons were wounded.

On 11 May 2022, gunmen abducted scores of commuters, including from a commercial vehicle they ambushed in around the Evekwu and Rumuodogo communities (Emohua, Rivers). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 11 May 2022, policemen and hunters clashed with armed individuals at Sara Kulinyi district (Hong, Adamawa) during an operation. Three armed men were killed, others fled with bullet wounds and one abductee was rescued.

On 11 May 2022, members of an unidentified cult militia attacked the home of a rival Aiye also known as Black Axe member and stabbed and injured his father in Badagry (Badagry, Lagos). The assailants were in search of their rival who was not at home when they arrived, his father was stabbed as a sign to show their presence.

On 11 May 2022, armed individuals numbering about five attacked a Muslim Cleric in a mosque at Kumo (Akko, Gombe) and set him ablaze. The assailants throw an explosive device at the cleric who was wounded along with some of his students. Some of the assailants were supporters of one of the aspirant for a legislative seats.

On 11 May 2022, policemen clashed with members of a Niger militia at Agigi/ Kpashimi forest in Lapai LGA (Niger). 15 abductees were freed, the militiamen fled into the bush with bullet wounds, two motorcycles were recovered and three militiamen were arrested by the policemen.

On 11 May 2022, armed individuals attacked a convoy of APC members, including a House of Assembly aspirant, at Italorun village on the Idanre-Akure road (Idanre, Ondo). The aspirant escaped unhurt, an unspecified number of others were wounded and taken to the hospital for treatment, vehicles were vandalized. The police claimed the attack was a result of a clash between two political aspirants in the area.

On 11 May 2022, members of a Zamfara militia shot at a vehicle and caused it to crash along Gusau Dansadau road (Gusau, Zamfara) and abducted one of its occupants, who is a journalist. The second person in the car escaped, the abductee was released around 17 May, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 11 May 2022, policemen, together with members of a local defense militia, clashed with armed individuals suspected to be abductors in Uzea forest, Esan Central LGA (Edo), coded to Irrua. Six persons were killed: two armed men on the spot and four others who were previously arrested and led the police to the hideout sustained gunshot injuries and died in the hospital. Weapons and ammunition were recovered by the police.

On 24 May 2022, members of a Benue communal militia engaged soldiers in an armed clash while they were being trailed by the soldiers after an abduction in Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). The abductee was rescued, three militiamen were killed, one rifle, three magazines, uniforms and phones were recovered by the soldiers.

On 24 May 2022, at least 8 members of a Katsina communal militia on four motorcycles attacked residents and shot sporadically at Gakurdi (Jibia, Katsina). 12 to 15 residents were killed and some farmlands were destroyed, sources report that the attack was a surprise attack related to the purchase of guns for the defense of the community by the Jibia Local Government Council.

On 24 May 2022, members of Black Axe also known as Aiye confraternity and Eiye confraternity members engaged in a supremacy battle in Ijaiye (Abeokuta North, Ogun). One militiaman was killed, the policemen were deployed to the area to restore order.

On 24 May 2022, armed individuals attacked an APC House of Representatives aspirant in Igosi, coded to Ilofa (Oke-Ero, Kwara). There were no casualties, the aspirant and his entourage were able to escape, he claimed the assailants were suspected to be from his political opponents.

On 24 May 2022, Black Axe militiamen also known as Aiye confraternity clashed with Eiye confraternity militiamen in reprisal for the killing of their member a few days earlier [coded separately] at Slaab and Amolasho areas of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) and Ijaiye [coded separately]. Two militiamen were killed.

On 24 May 2022, an Amotekun operative shot a civilian in the leg after he was arrested at Adigbe-Panseke road, Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The victim claimed that he was an onlooker at a road commissioning where he was arrested, and he was shot after an operative accused him of trying to escape from their office.
Around 24 May 2022 (as reported), armed individuals abducted one civilian from Angwan Gade, coded to Kuje (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductee was rescued by the police on 31 May [coded separately].
On 25 May 2022, unidentified gunmen ambushed a Nigerien police patrol near the village of Labau (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). Two policemen were killed, at least four wounded, and a vehicle burned.

On 25 May 2022, members of a Niger communal militia killed four PDP delegates between Mariga and Tegina (Mariga, Niger) while they were on their way home from Minna. The vehicle the victims were travelling in was shot at by the assailants; other sources report 3 fatalities, an unspecified number of others including the driver escaped.

On 25 May 2022, ISWAP claimed to have fired three mortar shells at an MNJTF checkpoint on the road between Fish Dam and Yarwa Bolin towns in the Lake Chad Basin, coded to Abadam (Abadan, Borno). Other sources claim the mortar shells landed in the bush without impact on the troops and the positions had previously been abandoned by the militants.

On 25 May 2022, members of a Katsina communal militia abducted two catholic priests and two other persons when they broke into rectory of a catholic church in Gidan Maikambo, Kafur LGA (Katsina). Other sources report that one politician was also abducted. The abductees were released around 26 June, Bishop Kukah claimed that a ransom of 30 million naira was paid for their release.
On 25 May 2022, armed individuals shot at commuters at Otite, along Okene-Lokoja highway (Okene, Kogi). Two persons were killed, the third person escaped unhurt.

On 26 May 2022, two groups of armed individuals who were supporters of APC politicians clashed at the venue of the house of assembly election in Mosun-Okunola (Alimosho, Lagos). Party members, electoral officers and security operatives fled the venue, the armed men took to the major road and fired gunshots, casualties are unknown.

On 26 May 2022, unidentified individuals abducted a female APC house of Assembly aspirant from Goergas community in Kwalla (Quan-Pan, Plateau). The abductee was travelling alongside her brother to meet with party delegates, he stopped to ask for directions and left her in the car but did only found her phones when he returned. There are no demands for ransom yet.

On 26 May 2022, armed men enforcing a sit in order beat up passengers of a tricycle and one motorcycle and set the vehicles ablaze in Nsukka (Nsukka, Enugu). The assailants shot sporadically in the air.

On 26 May 2022, armed individuals killed and wounded an unspecified number of supporters of a gubernatorial candidate of the APC at the venue of the primary elections in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano). The candidate claimed his supporters were killed an attempt was made to attack him, the police denied the claims and insisted there were no reports of violence at the venue. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 26 May 2022, armed individuals killed a soldier and one civilian and abducted a Lebanese engineer at Ogbonmo in Owo LGA (Ondo). The assailants shot into the air for several hours to scare residents and the murdered civilian was the driver of the vehicle.

On 26 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals kidnapped one member of the HYPPADEC governing council at Ogaminana (Adavi, Kogi). The victim was on his way to mosque when he was abducted; the abductee was released on 8 June, there are no reports on ransom payment. The police claimed he was abandoned by the abductors at a location from where he found his way home.

On 26 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals shot and killed a man who attempted to rescue a member of the HYPPADEC governing council who they abducted at Ogaminana (Adavi, Kogi). The victim was on his way to mosque when he was abducted; the murdered victim died three hours after he was shot, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 26 May 2022, Kogbagidi Boys and Willoughby Boys clashed in a supremacy battle at Ebute-Metta (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). The clash lasted for three days [coded separately], four persons were killed, residents in the area were robbed by the militiamen. Four fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 27 May 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia attacked civilians, killed 3 persons and cut off the hand of a 13 year old girl in Keku village, Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The girl died at the hospital due to bleeding, an unspecified number of persons were wounded.
On 27 May 2022, armed individuals shot and wounded two civilians along Laboard Road in Sapele LGA (Delta). One of the victims is a barber, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 27 May 2022 (between 27 - 28 May), troops of the MNJTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at Tunbun Rago and Tumbun Fulani in (Abadan, Borno) and Tumbun Dilla and Tumbun Jamina [coded separately]. The militants retreated and abandoned a three year old boy, one Civilian JFT fighter was killed.

On 27 May 2022, armed individuals abducted three persons travelling on the Kabba-Egbe road (Kabba, Kogi). The abductees were one nurse, a trader and a head master; a ransom of 20 million has been demanded for the release of the headmaster.

Around 27 May 2022 (between 27 - 28 May), troops of the MNJTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at Tumbun Dilla and Tumbun Jamina in Kukawa LGA (Borno) and Tumbun Rago and Tumbun Fulani [coded separately]. The Air Task Force was deployed to the location, scores of militants including a commander were killed, many others were wounded. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 27 May 2022, Kogbagidi Boys and Willoughby Boys clashed in a supremacy battle at Ebute-Metta (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). The clash lasted for three days [coded separately], four persons were killed, residents in the area were robbed by the militiamen. Four fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 28 May 2022, a group of armed hunters attacked a man and killed him in Lamurde LGA (Adamawa). The assailants inflicted injuries on the victim, and attacked the hospital where he was taken to; they took him to a bush, killed him and set his body ablaze. The reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 28 May 2022 (as reported), unidentified armed individuals killed one Boko Haram (JAS) militant who went to rustle cows around the axis of Konduga LGA (Borno). The militant's gun was recovered and handed over to the army.

Around 28 May 2022 (as reported), over 50 members of a Kaduna communal militia attacked, killed a man, abducted his pregnant wife and four others in Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). The other abductees were relatives of a former commissioner in the state and they were picked up in a house to house search; other sources report that the commissioner's house was targeted, the murdered victim was shot when he tried to resist the abduction of his wife.
On 28 May 2022, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants ambushed and killed two hunters who went hunting in Kaublin, Damboa LGA (Borno).

On 28 May 2022, Kogbagidi Boys and Willoughby Boys clashed in a supremacy battle at Ebute-Metta (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). The clash lasted for three days [coded separately], four persons were killed, residents in the area were robbed by the militiamen. Four fatalities split across 3 events coded as 1.

On 29 May 2022, armed individuals killed a retired air force officer and abducted two of his daughters from their residence in Azuba Bashayi, Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The victim was a relation to the state governor, a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded for the abductees' release, they were released on 1 June, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 29 May 2022, Ambazonian separatist fighters attacked and killed nearly 20 Cameroonians near Bashu (Boki, Cross River). The victims were persons who fled into Nigeria and refused to join the separatists, it unclear if any Nigerian was also killed. The Nigeria police has denied that the attack took place.

On 29 May 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted the chairman of a local defense militia in Ukwulu community (Dunukofia, Anambra). The abductee was returning from church when he was abducted, the abductees pointed a gun at him and shot into the air. There are no reports of ransom demands, the abductee was released at an unspecified date and there are no details about ransom payment.

On 29 May 2022, a suspected Fulani ethnic militia abducted a Methodist church leader and two other priests in Nneochi LGA (Abia) coded to Nkwoagu Isuochi. The abductees were abducted on their way from a church program, they were released on 30 May after a ransom of 100 million naira was paid. The Methodist leader claimed their abductors were Fulani pastoralists and that an army checkpoint was close by from where they were abducted.

On 29 May 2022, armed individuals shot and killed a policeman and took his rifle at Ogidi (Idemili North, Anambra). The assailants stationed themselves close to Ogidi Town Hall waiting until they sighted the policeman and fled after killing him.

On 30 May 2022, hunters clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) militants at Shaffu Taku village in Damboa LGA (Borno). One Boko Haram commander and his deputy were killed, several others escaped with bullet wounds, one rifle and a motorcycle were recovered by the hunters.

On 30 May 2022, suspected Igburra-Mozum ethnic militiamen attacked and killed two people assumed to be from Bassa ethnic group on a farm at Uga-Cheure, near Oguma (Bassa, Kogi) and Korumu [coded separately]. The attack is related to a communal clash over fish ponds and land ownership by Bassa and Ebira ethnic groups. Fatalities split across two events.
On 30 May 2022, IPOB militants killed a policeman at Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi).
On 30 May 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed a commercial motorcyclist in an unspecified location in Bayelsa state, coded to Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 30 May 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked Gidan Dan Inna (Bungudu, Zamfara), Gwaji and Karoka (coded separately). Scores of residents most of whom were local defense militiamen were killed, many others were abducted and four persons sustained varying degrees of injuries. Properties were also destroyed, 20 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 7.

On 30 May 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked Gwaji, Gidan Dan Inna (Bungudu, Zamfara), and Karoka (coded separately) . Scores of residents most of whom were local defense militiamen were killed, many others were abducted and four persons sustained varying degrees of injuries. Properties were also destroyed, 20 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 6.

On 30 May 2022, unidentified individuals armed with guns and machetes attacked a Fulani pastoralists camp and killed four persons at Ndiukwenu (Oji River, Enugu). The assailants also rustled 60 cattle, according to MACBAN cattle breeders association.

On 30 May 2022, armed individuals wounded a man when he tried to prevent them from abducting his son in Angwan Gade community, coded to Kuje (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victims' son was taken away by the assailants, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 30 May 2022, MNJTF troops repelled an attack by ISWAP militants on their formation at Arege (Abadan, Borno). The militants attacked the town from multiple flanks, one Hilux, an anti air craft gun ammunition and AK47 magazines were recovered by the troops who did not record any casualties, many militants were killed, coded as 3.

On 30 May 2022, unidentified armed individuals suspected to be cultists attacked and killed 4 persons including a commercial motorcyclist at Omoda/ Adangba quarters in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The fourth victim died from gunshot wounds a few days later, the police claimed one person was killed.

On 30 May 2022, two groups of Sara-Suka militiamen clashed against one another and one civilian was killed at Anguwan Rogo, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The civilian was returning home when he was stabbed by the Sara-Suka.

On 30 May 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked Karoka (Bungudu, Zamfara), and Gidan Dan Inna, Gwaji (coded separately). Scores of residents most of whom were local defense militiamen were killed, many others were abducted and four persons sustained varying degrees of injuries. Properties were also destroyed, 20 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 7.

On 30 May 2022, armed individuals wounded and brutalized the staff of Anambra Broadcasting Service when they attacked the station in Awada, Onitsha(Onisha North, Anambra). A building and two vehicles parked in the premises were burnt by the assailants.

On 30 May 2022, suspected Igburra-Mozum ethnic militiamen attacked and killed two people assumed to be from Bassa ethnic group on a farm at Korumu, near Odugbo (Bassa, Kogi) and Uga-Cheure [coded separately]. The attack is related to a communal clash over fish ponds and land ownership by Bassa and Ebira ethnic groups. Fatalities split across two events.

On 31 May 2022, policemen repelled an attack by members of a Kaduna militia who attacked Kimbi village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) in large numbers. Two militiamen were killed, two rifles were recovered several others sustained gunshot wounds.

On 31 May 2022, Nigerian troops raided a camp of Benue militiamen at killed two militiamen at Ahunga, Sati Mbachagh and Ayaghi village in Mbayongo (Katsina Ala, Benue). The militiamen fled after the sighted the troops and were chased, their camp was set ablaze.

On 31 May 2022, members of a Zamfara communal militia clashed with a local defense militia when they attacked Faru, Faru Magami ward, location coded to known village on the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). Scores of residents most of whom were local defense militiamen were killed, many others were abducted and four persons sustained varying degrees of injuries. Properties were also destroyed, 20 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 5.

On 31 May 2022, policemen and local defense militia men on patrol were ambushed and clashed with members of a Kaduna communal militia around Udawa (Chikun, Kaduna). The attack was repelled, the assailants fled with varying degrees of bullet wounds, left behind one rifle and four unregistered motorcycles.

On 31 May 2022, soldiers, policemen and DSS operatives raided a camp of IPOB militants who were dressed in military uniform and engaged them in a clash at Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The clash lasted for 30 minutes; three corpses of the assailants were recovered by the security operatives, 3-5 militants were killed some others fled with bullet wounds, two rifles and some rounds of ammunition were recovered.

On 31 May 2022, policemen beat up a woman who they accused of carrying sacrifice to the police station at Iwo (Iwo, Osun). The victim had gone to the police station to look for her missing son before the attack.

On 31 May 2022, policemen and hunters invaded the hideout of some armed men and engaged them in an armed clash at Dadu hills in Kuje LGA (FCT). One hunter was killed, the armed men fled with varying degrees of injuries. Several abductees were released.

On 31 May 2022, armed individuals and Nigerian Navy officers engaged in an armed clash which lasted for hours at Amiyi junction in Ochuche-Umuodo (Ogbaru, Anambra). The armed men were harassing road users before the officers accosted them, casualties are unknown.

On 31 May 2022, two rival groups of Zamfara militiamen clashed after the group loyal to Bello Turji attacked Dullu's group at their base in Shinkafi LGA (Zamfara). 17 to 44 militiamen from both groups were killed including the leader of the group; Dullu, some militiamen were abducted and later slaughtered by Turji, some others sustained bullet wounds, hundreds of animals were also rustled.

On 1 April 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked and killed at least 20 civilians in Daki Takwas village, Gummi LGA (Zamfara) and rustled hundreds of cattle. The police denied that the attack took place.

On 1 April 2022, policemen repelled an attack by an armed group on policemen attached to a construction company in Omege Noyo, (Ikwo, Ebonyi). One armed individual was killed, the others fled with bullet injuries; a policeman was wounded and left in a critical condition.

Around 1 April 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted seven persons related to the PDP chairman in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). One abductee was released earlier on health grounds, one was killed [coded separately] after the ransom demands were not met and the other 5 were released on 25 April, there are no reports about ransom payments.

Around 1 April 2022 (as reported), members of a Kaduna militia killed one of the seven abductees related to the PDP chairman of Kajuru LGA over the non-payment of ransom. Location coded to Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).
On 1 April 2022, suspected IPOB militants were repelled by policemen when they attacked a police divisional headquarters with IEDs in Mbieri (Mbaitoli, Imo ). There were no casualties.

On 1 April 2022, members of a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters, including two APC members, on the Anka-Zuru federal highway in Dajin Daki Takwas, Anka LGA (Zamfara). Nasiru Yari (APC), who was one of the abductees, was released on the same day after he paid 1.2 million naira to the militiamen. There are no reports about ransom demands for the other abductees.

On 1 April 2022, ISWAP militants killed four civilians in Sabon Tumbun (Kukawa, Borno). The victims were tried and convicted by the militants for various offenses including desertion and spying on the militants; they were also fishers accused of working with the Civilian JTF.

Around 1 April 2022 (as reported), soldiers on a clearance operation engaged over 400 Niger militiamen in an armed clash near Zuma Barrack, coded to nearby Suleja (Suleja, Niger). 14 soldiers and several militiamen were killed, several other soldiers were wounded. Several militia men deaths coded as 3. Fatalities coded as 17.

On 1 April 2022, an armed group attacked a police station and killed an unspecified number of policemen at Amichi (Nnewi South, Anambra). The police station was also set ablaze by the assailants. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 1 April 2022, members of a Katsina militia killed three traders and wounded an unspecified number when they invaded Yan Tumaki community market (Dan-Musa, Katsina). An unspecified number of persons were abducted; goods were stolen and destroyed by the assailants, the police claims one trader was killed and five others were wounded.
On 1 April 2022, an armed group in speed boats killed two persons and abducted three others when they attacked the Adobo housing scheme extension, in the Oshun area of Ayobo (Alimosho, Lagos).

On 1 April 2022, a navy officer attacked a man at a checkpoint around Owerri NTA Junction in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The man was killed in the attack. The man had refused to pay a bribe that led to an argument between the victim and the officers.

On 2 April 2022, an armed group abducted two teenage girls in Katsinawa village, Tudun Wada LGA (Kano) after the group abducted two teenage girls. The abductees were rescued following a clash with policemen and Yan Bula [coded separately].

On 2 April 2022, policemen and Yan Bula militiamen clashed with an armed group at the fringes of Falgore Forest, around Katsinawa village, Tudun Wada LGA (Kano) after the group abducted two teenage girls. The abductees were rescued. Three an armed group were killed; one of the bodies was set on fire by a mob. A weapon and ammunitions were seized by the police.
On 2 April 2022, Fulani militiamen attacked and killed ten civilians in Chando Zerreci village, Bassa LGA (Plateau). Nineteen other persons sustained gunshot wounds.
On 3 April 2022, an armed group killed seven persons and wounded 5 others in Tafi Gana village, Bassa (Plateau).

On 3 April 2022, an armed group, numbering about 1000, shot sporadically when they invaded Ifelodun community, Olorunsogo in Ifo LGA (Ogun) over a land dispute. The police denied the knowledge of any attack. There were no fatalities.
On 3 April 2022, Fulani militiamen attacked and killed two persons at Ritivo village, Bassa LGA (Plateau). Nine others sustained varying degrees of injuries.

On 3 April 2022, Ansaru militants clashed with militiamen in areas of Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna) and Tun Sado in Zamfara [coded separately]. A number of militiamen were killed, including a leader. One gun, 11 magazines and 15 motorcycles were seized by the militants. Ansaru claimed the clash. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 April 2022, an armed group invaded a mosque and abducted three persons, including an off duty policeman, at Soyoye (Abeokuta North, Ogun), coded to Akomoje. The policeman is also the chief imam of the mosque. A ransom of 5 million naira each was demanded for the abductees; the group was released after an unknown amount was paid. Other sources claim the police officer paid about 700 thousand naira as ransom.

On 3 April 2022, members of a Kaduna militia abducted two families and scores of almajiri from Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). Other sources report the number of abductees as 22, including 5 women. One abductee escaped while they were being taken into the bush, the abductors shot into the air to scare other residents from pursing them. There are no reports about demands for ransom.

On 3 April 2022, Ansaru militants clashed with militiamen in areas of Tun Sado, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) and Birnin Gwari in Kaduna [coded separately]. A number of militiamen were killed, including a leader. One gun, 11 magazines and 15 motorcycles were seized by the militants. Ansaru claimed the clash. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 April 2022, Nigerian Air Force and MNJTF carried out aerial and ground bombardment against ISWAP militants in Kwalaram village, Marte LGA (Borno). Dan-Buduma, an ISWAP commander and 19 others, including over a dozen of his lieutenants, were killed.

On 3 April 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked and killed three persons in Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara). One of the victims was the son of the state's commissioner for security and home affairs. Three other persons sustained gunshot wounds.

On 3 April 2022, an armed group attacked and killed two FRSC officials on duty along the Igbo-Ukwu-Ezinifite-Uga link road (Aguata, Anambra). One official escaped into the bush and one other sustained severe injuries from the attack.

On 4 April 2022, Hausa and Yoruba ethnic militias with cutlasses and other weapons clashed at Ipaja (Alimosho, Lagos) after a Hausa motorcyclist stabbed a Yoruba to death. At least 1 person killed. A motorcycle was burnt. The police intervened and brought the situation under control.
On 4 April 2022, Sokoto militiamen attacked a police checkpoint near Dogon Kare in Tureta LGA (Sokoto). One police personnel operation vehicle was set ablaze; casualties unknown.

On 4 April 2022, policemen shot and killed a man while he was eating at the Capital Area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Nigeria). The victim's friend and girlfriend were arrested; the girlfriend was later released. The police claimed they were acting on reports that criminals were in the area and clashed with the group which the victim was part of.

On 4 April 2022, large numbers of Kaduna militia members attacked a military base and clashed with soldiers and KADVS members in Polwire village, Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). Between 11 to 17 soldiers, 3 KADVS members and an unspecified number of militiamen were killed. 19 to 40 soldiers were wounded. The militiamen also had RPGs. They burned 2 to 3 armored personnel carriers and stole several weapons. Unknown fatalities coded as 3, total fatalities coded as 17.

On 4 April 2022, members of a Kaduna militia killed one civilian and abducted at least nine others, including a presumed off duty policewoman, in Kamazo (Chikun, Kaduna). The murdered victim was a commercial motorcycle rider, two of the policewoman's children were also abducted.

On 4 April 2022, soldiers and operatives of Amotekun corps clashed at Oke Aro area of Akure (Akure South, Ondo) after a dispute involving cattle grazing. Two Amotekun operatives were arrested by the soldiers; there were no casualties.

On 4 April 2022, an armed group, suspected to be supporters of Jacob Adebo (the new Chairman of the Vehicle Parks Management Committee), attacked NURTW members at various motor parks in Akure (Akure South, Ondo). Six NURTW members were wounded by the assailants who attacked with machetes, cutlasses, knives and other weapons.
On 4 April 2022, an armed group attacked and killed two private security men in Elwulobia (Aguata, Anambra). The victims were killed for attending a prayer session during the day's sit in order.
On 5 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed at least 3 persons in Ariri village (Bassa, Plateau). One person was also wounded and houses were set ablaze.

On 5 April 2022, an armed group numbering over 50 attacked Muslim worshippers while they were breaking their fast in a mosque at Baba Juli village, Bali LGA (Taraba). Three persons were killed, several other worshippers and villagers were abducted.

On 5 April 2022, policemen clashed with members of a Kaduna militia and foiled an attempted abduction at the Buruku - Birnin Gwari road (Chikun, Kaduna). The militiamen abandoned their victims and fled, there were no casualties.
On 5 April 2022, members of a Katsina militia killed a popular businessman, abducted his daughter and between 7 to 10 other persons from Gidan Daudu village in Kankara LGA (Katsina).

On 6 April 2022, an armed group abducted 16 passengers at Ojuwo-Ajegbo village (Ofu, Kogi), coded to Gwolawo. 12 of the abductees were rescued when the police chased after the abductors [there are no reports about a clash]; four abductees were yet to be found.

On 6 April 2022, suspected Fulani militiamen numbering six attacked IDPs who were trying to rebuild their homes at Rantis in Gashish district (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). Two persons were killed and three others sustained gunshot wounds; a car belonging to one of the victims was also burnt down.

On 6 April 2022, an armed group clashed with police and NSCDC during an attack on the venue of the SDP rally and the convoy of the gubernatorial candidate in Efon-Alaiye (Efon, Ekiti). One NSCDC operative was wounded, the assailants attacked the party supporters with stones, sticks and cutlasses and wounded some of them, vehicles in the convoy were damaged.
On 6 April 2022, policemen, with a reinforcement of soldiers, clashed with members of a Kaduna militia in Barakallahu (Igabi, Kaduna). The militiamen fled with varying degrees of bullet wounds.

On 6 April 2022, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants clashed with soldiers and Civilian JTF members when they attacked Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). The militants looted drugs and set part of a United Nations-supported primary healthcare center and a Technical girls college ablaze. They parked their motorcycles behind a trench dug around the town and entered on foot. Two Civilian JTF members were wounded.
On 7 April 2022, members of a Niger militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians when they raided Daza community (Muya, Niger).

On 7 April 2022, suspected armed pastoralists attacked the Odiguetue community (Ovia North East, Edo) and killed 5 persons. The community leader claimed the assailants had repeatedly invaded the community and destroyed the locals' crops to feed their cattle.

On 7 April 2022, members of Sukuku local defense militia clashed with an armed group while trying to rescue abductees in Sukuku (Kwali, FCT). Two local defense militiamen were killed; three others were wounded, an unspecified number of armed men were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3, total fatalities coded as 5.

On 7 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed five persons, including the Gwagwalad area council chairman of MACBAN, near Daku village in Dobi ward (Gwagwalada, FCT). Three to four other persons were abducted and three persons were wounded; other sources report several persons wounded.

On 7 April 2022, members of a Niger militia, numbering over 50, killed 3 persons, including a village head and a Fulani pastoralist, when they attacked Dazza, Dandaudu, Fukan, Gwari, Maraban Zagzaga (Muya, Niger) and Zagzaga [coded separately]. An unspecified number of persons were abducted, cattle were rustled. Fatalities divided into two events and coded as 2.

On 7 April 2022, members of a Niger militia, numbering over 50, killed 3 persons, including a village head and a Fulani pastoralist, when they attacked Zagzaga (Muya, Niger), Dandaudu, Fukan, Gwari, Maraban Zagzaga and Dazza [coded separately]. An unspecified number of persons were abducted, cattle were rustled. Fatalities divided into two events coded as 1.
On 7 April 2022, members of the Niger militia attacked civilians in Rumache - Madalla (Shiroro, Niger). Three persons were killed; several others were wounded and many others were abducted.

On 7 April 2022, presumed Sukuku local defense militiamen killed an unspecified number of armed individuals attempting to evacuate the corpses of their members to a hideout at a forest in or around Lanto village (Kuje, FCT). The local defense militiamen had engaged the armed men at Sukuku [coded separately] which led to the killing of members whose corpses were being evacuated. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 7 April 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked residents and killed two persons in Ariko (Kachia, Kaduna), which is a Fulani settlement. A man and two of his children were abducted.

On 7 April 2022, Black Axe, also called Aiye militia, attacked and killed a member of Eiye confraternity in Somolu (Somolu, Lagos). The victim was macheted and shot over a long standing rivalry between the two groups.

On 7 April 2022, an armed group killed 2 - 'many' persons when they invaded the local government headquarters in Elwulobia (Aguata, Anambra). Structures, shops and vehicles within the secretariat were set ablaze. Fatalities coded as 2.
