On 19 April 2022, Zamfara militiamen fired indiscriminately when they attacked civilians at Sabon Gari, Bakura LGA (Zamfara). One person was killed, five others were wounded and an unspecified number of cattle were rustled.

On 19 April 2022, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with Zamfara militiamen around Kurunkudu forest in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). At least 10 militiamen were killed and an unspecified number sustained gunshot wounds.

On 19 April 2022, an armed group abducted a televangelist from his church in Ibekwe Akpanya (Mkpat Enin, Akwa Ibom). The abductors demanded for a ransom of 100 million naira and reduced it to 30 million. The abductee was released on 22 April, there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 19 April 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted an off duty NCoS official along the Kaduna road, coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna). A ransom of 20 million naira was demanded, the abductee was released after 1.2 million naira was paid.

On 19 April 2022, suspected members of a Zamfara militia shot at commuters when the driver of the vehicle refused to stop at the Anka-Dakitwakwas-Gummi axis (Anka, Zamfara). A secondary school teacher who was in the vehicle was killed.

On 19 April 2022, Boko Haram (JAS faction) fighters ambushed ISWAP fighters in Yale village, Damboa LGA (Borno) and Gargash (coded separately) while they were moving to a new camp around Alafa axis at night. In Yale, 2 ISWAP Khaids and 4 fighters were killed, 4 others were captured and killed, while three vehicles were seized.

On 19 April 2022, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians in Malali (Illela, Sokoto), Gati, Koringo, Munwadata, Mullela Tarke and Tudungudale [coded separately]. 12 persons were killed, fatalities split across five events coded as 3.

On 19 April 2022, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated to the deputy chairman of Isiala Ngwa North council attacked and disrupted PDP stake holders consultation meeting in Okpuala-Ngwa (Isiala Ngwa, Abia). The attack followed a verbal attack by the deputy chairman on a governorship aspirant.

On 19 April 2022, gunmen ambushed the convoy of a House of Representatives member in Miango (Bassa, Plateau). Two persons who were leaders in the PDP, and were on a motorcycle, first encountered the ambush and were killed; the lawmaker's car was battered with bullets, he and his family and other members of the convoy escaped.
On 19 April 2022, gunmen killed a pregnant woman and abducted two of her children and a Christian pastor from Dadin Kowa, Jos South (Plateau), coded to Bukuru.

On 19 April 2022, Nigerian troops clashed with an armed group in Chito (Ukum, Benue) and killed three armed individuals. An undisclosed number of weapons, two motorcycles and three phones were recovered.

On 19 April 2022, Nigerian troops on an offensive patrol clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists in Atunbe, Madamu, Kaamen, Ude -Jor, Kasar, Tor-Tacha and River Yoyo in Katsina Ala LGA (Benue), coded to Katsina-Ala. The militiamen fled with possible bullet wounds, firearms and cutlasses were recovered after a search around the area by the troops.

Around 19 April 2022, Boko Haram (JAS faction) fighters ambushed ISWAP militants at Gargash (Bama, Borno) and Yale [coded separately]. At least 32 militants from both sides were killed in the two clashes, with 10 fatalities in Yale (coded separately) Remaining fatalities of at least 22 coded in Gargash.

On 20 April 2022, hunters clashed with an armed group suspected to be abducting civilians along Okele-Ochadam road (Ofu, Kogi). Two from the armed group were killed, three others sustained gunshot wounds.

Around 20 April 2022 (between 20 - 21 April), Nigerian troops clashed with an armed group at Agam/Gidan Bawa village (Nassarawa, Kano) while responding to a distress call regarding an attempted abduction. Five abductees were rescued from an abductors camp, the leader of the group was arrested.

On 20 April 2022, policemen repelled an attack by armed individuals at a police station in Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra). The assailants threw bonfires inside the station; three police operational vehicles were destroyed, there were no casualties on the part of the police, the assailants fled and casualties are unknown.
On 20 April 2022, Nigerian troops mistakenly killed three civilians during an operation against militiamen in Kwatan Nanido (Gassol, Taraba).

On 20 April 2022, policemen engaged members of a Niger militia in an armed clash, as the militiamen attacked Galiwi village via Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). 13 farmers who were abducted were rescued unhurt, the militiamen fled and there were no casualties.

On 20 April 2022, the Nigeria Air Force carried out airstrikes and were supported ground troops against armed group camps around Kambari (Karim Lamidu, Borno). Many militiamen were killed, an unspecified number of others, including their informants, were arrested by the ground troops around Gassol and Karim Lamido. Unknown fatalities coded as 10.

On 20 April 2022, armed individual shot and killed three persons at their duty post where they were collecting parking fees in Uselu-Nahor, coded to Ehor (Uhunmwode, Edo). The attack is related to leadership crisis in the area. Other sources reported that the assailants were masked and four persons including the head of the town's security was killed while residents fled from the area.

Around 20 April 2022 (as reported), troops of the MNJTF supported by the air task force carried out offensives against ISWAP/Boko Haram militants in the vicinities of Tunbun Fulani and Tunbun Rago (Abadan, Borno) and Marte LGA [coded separately]. About 20 militants and one soldier were killed around Tunbun Rago, a few soldiers were wounded during the operations; the militants fled and left weapons, their uniforms and other equipment's behind. A shallow grave with Boko Haram corpses was discovered, six female abductees who escaped during the operations were rescued.

Around 20 April 2022 (as reported), the MNJTF claimed its troops carried out clearance operations against ISWAP/Boko Haram in the vicinity of Toumbuma, Kerenua and Chikul Gudu, coded to Marte (Marte, Borno) and Abadan LGA [coded separately]. Two suspected ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and one soldier was killed around Marte and a few others were wounded in the clearance operations.

On 20 April 2022, around two dozen ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants dressed in military uniform attacked and killed civilians in parts of Geidam (Geidam, Yobe). Bewteen 11 to 22 persons were killed; 9, including two women and a retired police officer, were killed at a bar. Two others were killed at the government technical school and some buildings there were burnt.

On 20 April 2022, a large number of Boko Haram fighters led by Ambu Mairamiri invaded an ISWAP settlement and engaged them in an armed clash near Ngurosoye (Bama, Borno). 18 ISWAP and 6 Boko Haram fighters were killed, four ISWAP gun trucks and newly erected makeshift tents were destroyed.

On 20 April 2022, a team of soldiers and policemen repelled members of a Katsina militia as they attacked civilians in Dusten Reme Low-Cost, Funtua LGA (Katsina). Two civilians were killed before the arrival of security operatives.
On 20 April 2022, a police DPO shot and killed a man at a pub in Urualla (Ideato North, Imo). The attack was caused by a disagreement over vehicle parking.

On 20 April 2022, members of a Katsina militia on motorcycles killed a councilor in Gozaki community (Kafur, Katsina) when they attacked the community. The victim's two wives were first abducted by the militiamen who returned them and sprayed his body with bullets.
On 20 April 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and Nigerian troops engaged in an armed clash at Buduwa (Bama, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.
On 20 April 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked Nigerian troops stationed at Kurnari (Biu, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.
On 20 April 2022, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked civilians in Wulgo town (Ngala, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.
On 20 April 2022, members of a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians from Dan Rimi community in Malumfashi LGA (Katsina), Residents of the community have fled the area.

On 21 April 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked a local defense militia on patrol in Manini (Chikun, Kaduna). The commander of the defense militia was wounded, their patrol vehicle was set ablaze.

On 21 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians on their farm in Waya community (Kwande, Benue). Between 8 to 11 people, five of whom were from the same family, were killed. More victims were still being searched for, an unspecified number were wounded.
On 21 April 2022, unidentified armed individuals shot and killed a Fulani pastoralist in Rangyel community, Bassa LGA (Plateau). Four cows were killed and five others were wounded.

On 21 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians in Tse Ibe, Tse Katsa, Tse Melayongu and Mbaakpam in Mbapa ward (Gwer West, Benue) and in Mbabuande [coded separately]. Nine persons were killed in the attack, the assailants killed only men, the victims' bodies were mutilated.

On 21 April 2022, Nigerian troops foiled an attack by ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants on a military formation guarding trenches in Malari (Guzamala, Borno). Many residents fled into the city center for safety, casualties unknown.

On 21 April 2022, Cameroonian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at Wulgo (Ngala, Borno). 2 militants were killed, one soldier was wounded and the militants were repelled. The clash started in the night and lasted till 2am the following day.

On 21 April 2022, policemen repelled an attack by Katsina militiamen and killed two militiamen in Tsamiyar Gamzako village, Kafur LGA (Katsina). An abductee and her baby were rescued, other militiamen fled, weapons and ammunition were recovered.

Around 21 April 2022, (between 18 April and 24 April), an unidentified armed group killed around five Aro Bagger militia members in Over Rail Aba (Aba South, Abia). The bodies were dumped in different parts of the area, some sources report that the killings which took place over one week was not related to a cult war, around five others were killed on 25 April [coded separately].

On 21 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians in Tse Agungu Unger, coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue) and in Mbapa ward [coded separately]. Three persons were killed in the attack, the assailants killed only men.

On 22 April 2022, armed individuals abducted a student, who is also the son of a senior legislative aide of the deputy senate president, in Abraka (Ethiope East, Delta). A ransom of 50 million naira, which was later reduced to 3 million was demanded; the abductee was released on 25 April, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 22 April 2022, NDLEA operatives on patrol shot and killed one man in Sundimina (Birnin Kudu, Jigawa). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 22 April 2022, a Niger Communal Militia abducted 13 farmers from a farm in Galiwi village, along the Sarkin Pawa road (Muya, Niger).

On 22 April 2022, armed individuals killed two Christian teenagers when they entered the house of a retired police officer during a wedding ceremony at the Hausa community of Gudum Hausawa (Bauchi, Bauchi). Wedding attendees were beat and wounded. The reason for the attack is unknown, although the event has been reported within a communal crisis context between the community and a Fulani community.

On 22 April 2022, armed individuals numbering about 40 abducted 10 MACBAN members and stole 300 cows in Obene (Ogbaru, Anambra). A ransom of 4 million naira and one gun was demanded. On 24 April, an unspecified number of the abductees and some of the cattle were found by the police [no interaction reported].

On 22 April 2022, ISWAP / Boko Haram militants attacked civilians at a wedding and coronation ceremony and shot sporadically in Kidindila village, coded to Askira (Askira Uba, Borno). At least one person was killed; several others were wounded; the murdered victim was a member of the local defense militia, he was taken away and his body was later recovered. The assailants arrived in two gun trucks and blocked the exit of the occasion.

On 22 April 2022, NURTW members and TOOAN members loyal to Istijaba clashed at Meiran-Ijaiye axis and Ekoro road in Abule Egba (Alimosho, Lagos) using guns, charms and other weapons. One road side trader was hit and wounded by a stray bullet.

On 22 April 2022, policemen from the Edo state command shot and killed a member of the local defense militia (presumed unarmed) at his residence in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The policemen were invited by a couple who had a disagreement with the victim, he was killed following a war of words with the policemen. The policemen and couple were arrested.

Around 23 April 2022 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed a businessman they abducted along the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The victim was abducted with 8 others who were released, a ransom was paid for the release of all the abductees and an additional 20 million [which was not paid] was demanded for the killed victim.
On 23 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian troops at the outskirts of Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). There are no further details. Casualties unknown.

On 23 April 2022, ISWAP clashed with police when they attacked a police station from different directions at Ogaminana (Adavi, Kogi). Three policemen were killed, the assailants fled with gunshot wounds, ISWAP claimed the attack.

On 23 April 2022, a member of the local defense militia shot and wounded nine children at Ogida quarters, Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The children were playing football before the assailant shot them, he claimed to have warned them to stop playing football after they had previously destroyed his property with their ball.
On 23 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists ambushed and killed a farmer in Unguwar Wereng (Riyom, Plateau) on his way from Farin Lamba.

On 24 April 2022, soldiers at a checkpoint clashed with armed individuals who invaded the area in 3 boats at Ogboinbiri (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The soldiers were guarding a wellhead owned by SPDC; one assailant was killed, one soldier was wounded and his rifle was stolen.

On 24 April 2022, an armed group, numbering over 100, attacked residents of Adagba in Yaba ward (Abaji, FCT). Two persons were killed, including a nine year old girl who was initially declared missing; seven persons were abducted and 36 motorcycles were stolen. 10 of the stolen motorcycles were recovered from Zago community after they ran out of fuel and were abandoned by the assailants. The abductees, with 10 others, were rescued by a local defense militia in Zago community around 13 May.
On 24 April 2022, ISWAP fighters attacked dozens of Boko Haram (presumed JAS faction) fighters, clashing with them, in Tokombere (Gwoza, Borno). A Boko Haram commander, Mohammed Reejal, was killed.

On 24 April 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted 3 persons near Kasuwan Magani (Kajuru, Kaduna) including a woman, her daughter and a commercial driver who were returning to Kaduna; a ransom of 100 million was demanded for the two women. The woman was released, the daughter and driver were released about three weeks later, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 24 April 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted three firefighters and released them in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) after a ransom of 5 million naira was paid around 27 April.

On 25 April 2022, IPOB/ ESN militants clashed with Nigerian troops on a routine patrol along the Orlu-Orsu road (Orlu, Imo). Two militants were killed, four others were arrested; one rifle, two magazines one police grenade launcher and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 25 April 2022, a Kaduna militia killed an APC ward chairman and several others when they attacked several communities in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). Scores of residents were abducted, others were seriously wounded, some cows and household animals were seized. The ward chairman was hit by a stray bullet and he died on the spot, several fatalities coded as 3. Total fatalities coded as 4.

On 25 April 2022, policemen clashed with a Katsina militia that attacked civilians at Garin Zaki, Batsari LGA (Katsina). Three abductees were rescued and 15 rustled cows were recovered. Casualties unknown.

On 25 April 2022, Nigerian troops in conjunction with Civilian JTF on a joint clearance operation invaded the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Tesa village, Dikwa LGA (Borno), Mallam Maja and Gosoma [coded separately]. About 39 militants were killed, eight guns and four gun trucks were seized. Fatalities split across 3 events coded as 13.

On 25 April 2022, Nigerian troops in conjunction with Civilian JTF on a joint clearance operation invaded the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Gosoma (Dikwa, Borno), Mallam Maja and Tesa [coded separately]. About 39 militants were killed, eight guns and four gun trucks were seized. Fatalities split across 3 events coded as 13.

On 25 April 2022, Nigerian troops in conjunction with Civilian JTF on a joint clearance operation invaded the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Mallam Maja (Dikwa, Borno), Gosoma and Tesa [coded separately]. About 39 militants were killed, eight guns and four gun trucks were seized. Fatalities split across 3 events coded as 13.

On 25 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked civilians in Kangara village, Gubio LGA (Borno) and killed at least one person. Many residents were wounded, many others fled into the bushes for safety.

On 25 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram killed a man, burnt his house and stole his livestock at Bujimirum, also called Katarko (Gujba, Yobe). The militants claimed to have captured and killed a spy of the Nigerian army.

On 25 April 2022, an unidentified armed group killed over five Aro Bagger militia members while enforcing a sit in order in Over Rail and other parts of Aba (Aba South, Abia). The bodies were dumped in different parts of the area. Some sources report that the killings which took place over one week was not related to a cult war.
On 25 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed 25 civilians at Kamaru ward (Kauru, Kaduna).

On 25 April 2022, police officers shot sporadically when they invaded the Imo state command of the NSCDC in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The clash resulted from a disagreement between a police officer dressed in mufti and NSCDC operatives. One NSCDC operative was killed, the commandant was beaten up and arrested by the police officers.

On 25 April 2022, an armed group took over the streets and shot sporadically in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). Residents scampered for safety; officers of the custodial center barricaded the center to avoid an incursion. Casualties unknown.

On 26 April 2022, policemen responded to a distress call and repelled an attack by Katsina militiamen in Kadage village, Kurfi LGA (Katsina). One militiaman was killed, all the rustled animals were recovered; many militiamen fled with gunshot wounds.

On 26 April 2022, soldiers and Civilian JTF engaged Kaduna militiamen in an armed clash after the militiamen invaded Angwa Kadara in Juji (Chikun, Kaduna). Some unarmed youths in the area confronted and chased the militiamen before they were intercepted by soldiers and CJTF. One woman was killed and another was abducted. Three persons, including the commander of the Civilian JTF, sustained bullet wounds from the attack which lasted till the following morning.

On 26 April 2022, Nigerian troops in conjunction with the Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram fighters during a clearance operation at Kasha in Mafa LGA (Borno). Six militants were killed, weapons and ammunition, amongst others items were recovered.

On 26 April 2022, Nigerian troops on a clearance operation destroyed Boko Haram/ ISWAP enclaves around Merkas and Yarganari villages, coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed and abducted victims were rescued. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 26 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed a Fulani pastoralist who was tending to cows in Ogu community (Ogu, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 26 April 2022, Oyo State Park Management System clashed with Isota boys and Were boys at the Ali Iwo area of Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). Some sources claim the clash was a result of the sporadic shooting by members of the Park Management System which resulted in the death of one person hit by a stray bullet; some reports mentioned that the Isota and Were boys attacked passers-by, especially persons wearing cloths with the governor or PMS insignia. At least three persons were killed in total, scores were wounded and vehicles were vandalized.

On 27 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians in Kitakum, Ungwan Magaji and Ungwan Rimi in Kauru LGA (Kaduna). About 22 persons were killed, 19 of whom were from the Irigwe ethnic group, several others were injured and 60 houses were burnt.

On 27 April 2022, armed individuals killed a member of NNPP in Bayelsa state at his residence around Bay-Bridge road in Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The assailants shot the victim several times through the window of his bedroom after they scaled the perimeter fence of the house. The victim was a former APC chieftain before he defected to the NNPP.

On 27 April 2022, policemen and members of a local defense militia clashed with Katsina militiamen and repelled them from Marina village in Safana LGA (Katsina). One of the assailants were killed; a gun and two of their motorcycles were recovered.
On 27 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and wounded two Fulani pastoralists around Kpara village (Bassa, Plateau). Six cattle were shot dead, at least 113 others were rustled.
On 27 April 2022, a Kaduna militia shot and injured a doctor who attempted to escape abduction, together with other people, along the Kaduna-Abuja road, coded to Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna).

On 27 April 2022, an assumed Fulani militia, killed one person in the Hausa community of Gudum Hausawa (Bauchi, Bauchi) during the burial of two other people killed on the previous week (coded separately). 20 houses were burnt. The event happens within the context of communal clashes between Fulani and Hausa in the region and the attack was described as an reprisal attack to the previous week one.

On 27 April 2022, armed individuals suspected to be assassins attacked the residence of an APC chieftain, wounded a gatekeeper, and bound the others in the Nasarawa area of Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano). The assailants did not gain access into the house; the police were alerted by neighbors. The chieftain is also a gubernatorial aspirant in Jigawa state and he was not in the house at the time of the attack, other sources report that the gatekeeper was shot and wounded.

On 27 April 2022, MNJTF troops with air support clashed with ISWAP/Boko Haram militants at Tunbun Rago (Abadan, Borno) and killed at least 20 militants. 12 rifles, a large cache of ammunitions, 5 gun trucks laden with supplies and a MRAP were recovered by the troops.

Around 27 April 2022 (as reported), MNJTF troops from Cameroon on a clearance patrol came in contact with two Boko Haram militants [presumed JAS] at the general area of Chikulgudu, coded to Wulgo (Ngala, Borno). The militants were killed and two motorcycles were recovered.

On 27 April 2022, suspected Ikot Ekwere militiamen raped women when they invaded Ikot Obio Offong community coded to Nung Udoe (Ibesikpo Asutan, Akwa Ibom). The assailants burnt a car, over 20 houses, wounded many people, looted household items, domestic animals and money from other houses. They chanted war songs and fired several gunshots; two persons were missing up till June, the attack was over a protracted land dispute.

On 28 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked two locals working on their farm and killed them at Tse Tume in Turan council ward (Logo, Benue). Other sources claim three victims, including one woman, was killed.

On 28 April 2022, a Kaduna militia abducted the village head of Rijana and an unspecified number of farmers at Kurmi community, coded to Rijana (Kachia, Kaduna). The abductors demanded for tramadol, gallons of petrol, engine oil, cigarettes, recharge cards and two new motorcycles as ransom.

On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops on a clearance operation killed several ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, including the spiritual head of Galta, around Manjo Ali Qere, Dikwa LGA (Borno). Arms and ammunition were also recovered; several fatalities coded as 3.

On 28 April 2022, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed two loggers who were IDPs from the Mandarari camp, their bodies were found near Konduga LGA (Borno). The victims were assumed by the militants to be spies of the military.
On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops, after sighting ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, shelled around the Dalori area (Jere, Borno) and the Molai General area [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.
On 28 April 2022, Nigerian troops, after sighting ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants, shelled around Molai General area (Jere, Borno) and around Dalori [coded separately]. Casualties unknown.

On 28 April 2022, local defense militiamen from a community in Oyigbo LGA attacked locals from Oloko community working on a community farmland in Tai LGA (Rivers), on the boundary between Oloko and Afam and coded to Ogoni. The assailants killed a pastor, abducted an unspecified number of persons, burnt houses and the victim's motorcycle.

On 28 April 2022, soldiers responded to a distress call and repelled an attack on civilians by an armed group at Rikwe-Chongu village in Kwal district (Bassa, Plateau). Between 2 to 3 civilians and one soldier were killed; one person was wounded and several houses were burned, food barns were destroyed, food stuff and domestic animals were stolen.

On 28 April 2022, armed individuals with machetes attacked security guards and residents at 2/1 New Site in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Many residents and some guards were wounded and robbed. The assailants, whom arrived in motorcycles, were invited by a commercial tricycle rider in retaliation after he was beaten by a resident earlier.

On 28 April 2022, suspected cult militiamen attacked and injured a human right activist at the Alex Ekueme Square in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants, numbering about 11, wielded guns and other weapons and invaded the venue while tricycle operators were waiting to meet the governor; police operatives intervened and shot in the air before the assailants left.
On 28 April 2022, armed individuals ambushed, shot and wounded a pregnant woman between Kaseyo and Torkula villages (Guma, Benue). The victim was returning to Gbajimba when the attack took place.

On 29 April 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed five civilians at a bar at Obiofia village in Osumenyi (Nnewi South, Anambra). The owner of the joint and four customers were the victims, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno), as well as Dipchari, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Bula Musa, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, (Bama, Borno), Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, Bomari, as well as Dipchari, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, and Dar el Jamal [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Kote (Bama, Borno), as well as Jeree, Gargash, Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 4.

On 29 April 2022, Nigerian troops with air support repelled an attack by ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). The militants, in two groups, attacked the town from Magumeri road and Gubio road; many militants were killed and several others were wounded before they retreated. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 29 April 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with NSCDC operatives providing security coverage to the Livestock Guards at the Wadata axis of Makurdi LGA (Benue). Two NSCDC operatives and one livestock guard were killed, and one operative was wounded. The operatives had seized some cows violating the open grazing law before they were ambushed by the group.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Dipchari (Bama, Borno), as well as Dar el Jamal, Gargash, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Gargash (Bama, Borno), as well as Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Jeree, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 4.

Around 29 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops on a clearance operation clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and cleared their hideouts at Jeree (Bama, Borno), as well as Gargash, Dipchari, Dar el Jamal, Kote, Bula Musaye, Bula Moruye, Bula Dalo, Landarari, Boroshem, Yamut, and Bomari [coded separately]. Scores of militants were killed; over 500 women, children and abductees were rescued. 20 fatalities split across 6 events coded as 3.

On 30 April 2022, policemen clashed with armed individuals who attempted to abduct an expatriate in Ovia North East LGA (Edo), coded to Okada. Five of the assailants were killed, others escaped with bullet wound, two guns and eight live cartridges were recovered.

On 30 April 2022, armed individuals ambushed and killed 5 commuters along the Sabon Gari-Kampani road, Wase LGA (Plateau). The victims include a member of a local defense militia (presumed unarmed) whose motorcycle was stolen after he was killed, and locals returning from the market. 20 other persons were abducted.

Around 30 April 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops from Benue and Taraba clashed with armed Fulani militiamen at Kashimbila (Takum, Tarab) during a patrol. One militiaman was killed, the others fled with varying degrees of wounds and left a teenager boy behind. The troops set the militia's makeshift camp ablaze and recovered 4 cutlasses, one knife and other weapons.

On 30 April 2022, suspected IPOB militants raped a woman, and killed her and her husband close to the Banana junction in Orlu (Orlu, Imo) as they were on their way to Imo for their wedding. On 15 March 2022, armed individuals clashed with NDLEA officers, backed up by police and military, during an attack to the NDLEA offices in Ntezi (Ishielu, Ebonyi). Four people were killed: two armed individuals, a NDLEA officer and a patient from the agency's rehabilitation center. Other armed individuals escaped with injuries.

On 15 March 2022, armed individuals clashed with police officers in Gafara, Ngaski LGA (Kebbi), coded to Wara, after crossing to the region from the Danko/Wasagu LGA (Kebbi). Four police officers and between 1 to 7 civilians were killed. The group of about 500 armed men took over a tomato company in the area.

On 15 March 2022, militiamen clashed with the police and local vigilantes during an attack in Nasko (Magama, Niger). Three police officers and four local defense militia members were killed, along with seven militiamen. The attack would be in retaliation to another clash which left several militiamen killed and 800 cattle recovered (coded separately).

On 15 March 2022, armed individuals killed four people and abducted four others, including the Maigemu village head, during attacks in Kwatan Nanido, Maigemu, Tinga, Kwamishina Maigemu villages in Gassol LGA (Taraba), coded to Mutum Biyu.

Around 15 March 2022 (between 14 - 16 March), four people, including two local defense militia members, were killed by suspected cult militia members at the Boboroku and Irodo communities of the Idjerhe kingdom in Jesse (Ethiope West, Delta). The event happens within the context of rivalry clashes between two cult militias.
On 15 March 2022, the police killed three suspected kidnappers at their hideout in Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta).

On 15 March 2022, suspected ISWAP members abducted a doctor in Gubio (Gubio, Borno). The group also seized food stuff and fuel from an humanitarian truck. The abductee was released around 18 February 2023, after he was forced to treat wounded militants and their families, there are no reports about ransom payment.
Around 15 March 2022 (as reported), Aro and Bobo cult militias clashed in Aba (Aba South, Abia) following the killing of an Aro member (details not specified). 3 people were killed.

On 15 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen attacked civilians, killed three persons and abducted eight others along the Dogon Dawa- Zaria road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 15 March 2022, cult militia members attacked UNIZIK vigilante members at the Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The police arrested an unspecified number of cultist members.
On 15 March 2022, two bus drivers were killed by officers from the Lagos State Task Force in Isheri (Kosofe, Lagos). Circumstances for the deaths are unknown.

On 16 March 2022, a woman was kidnapped by three armed individuals from her house in Ishiagu (Aniocha South, Delta). She had been previously kidnapped in 2019, and released - at the time - after the payment of ransom.
On 16 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed a school teacher at Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 16 March 2022, joint security operatives comprised of military, police and Niger State Vigilante Group members clashed with militiamen at the group's hideouts in or around Bangi (Mariga, Niger). A police officer was killed and the state's Commissioner claimed that over 100 militiamen were killed and 50 motorcycles were seized from the group. The operation took place following a discovered plan to attack the village and after the Nasko clash (coded separately). Fatalities coded as 101.

On 16 March 2022, armed individuals abducted 8 persons, including 3 women APC ward leaders, travelling in separate buses between Araromi-Opin and Obbo Ile (Ekiti, Kwara). Five of the abductees escaped, the women leaders and three other men were held by the abductors who demanded a ransom of 20 million naira. The abductee were rescued by a local defense militia (coded separately).

On 16 March 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty policeman as he was returning home from work in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The abductee was rescued the following day at Umueze in Awkunanaw. There are no reports of a clash or ransom payment.
On 16 March 2022, a Zamfara militia raped women and rustled cattle when they invaded Dutsin Zai and Gamawa in Tofa district (Bungudu, Zamfara).
On 17 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen abducted two men from Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 17 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen killed one man and abducted seven women at Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 17 March 2022 (as reported), Adadama militiamen killed a man in Ochanyim Amagu (Ikwo, Ebonyi) within the context of land disputes of the community with the Adadama community in Cross Rivers state.

On 17 March 2022, policemen and soldiers in collaboration with a local defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group at Dobi Kwalita, coded to Dobi (Gwagwalada, FCT). One abductee was rescued, and one of the assailants were arrested, two guns that were loaded with ammunition were recovered by the security operatives.

Around 17 March 2022 (between 10 - 24 March), soldiers engaged Kaduna militiamen in an armed clash after airstrikes by the air force in Magaba (Giwa, Kaduna), according to the Defence headquarters. 8 militiamen were killed, 7 were arrested.
On 17 March 2022, a pastoralist was killed by armed individuals presumably in Kaura LGA (Kaduna), coded to Kaura. 30 cows were also killed and 7 motorcycles were burnt.
On 17 March 2022, armed individuals shot and killed the vice chairman of the Borno chapter of Timber Shed Association in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 17 March 2022, ISWAP/Boko Haram members clashed with the military during an attack to a base in Bama (Bama, Borno). One soldier was killed, several were injured and a number of them are missing. The group took over the military base.
On 17 March 2022, militia members shot and injured one person and kidnapped between 48 to 57 people (including 32 women) in Agunu Dutse community (Kachia, Kaduna).

Around 17 March 2022 (as reported), NURTW member assaulted with cutglass and sticks, and injured Fire Service members in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) after arriving at their premises in three vehicles. 10 Fire Service staff were severely injured. Motivation for the attack is unknown.
On 17 March 2022, a Zamfara militia raped women and rustled cattle when they invaded Dan Daji and Dakace in Tofa district (Bungudu, Zamfara).

On 18 March 2022, a suspected members of an unidentified cult militia killed a man at Baruwa estate (Alimosho, Lagos). The victim's body was found with marks that indicated he was attacked with a cutlass, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 18 March 2022, armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with farmers at Magirami bush in Guri LGA (Jigawa). Two persons were killed and five others were wounded, other sources report at least 5 to 6 persons killed and many others wounded.

On 18 March 2022, armed individuals killed the step-brother of an aide to the Plateau state governor in Takas village, Pankshin LGA (Plateau). The aide's stepmother and a girl leaving with her were abducted, there are no reports of ransom demands.

On 18 March 2022, DSS operatives shot sporadically and killed one woman at Ologo, Coal Camp, (Enugu North, Enugu). The victim was pursued and shot by one of the operatives, the reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 18 March 2022 (as reported), the military claimed a clash with ISWAP/Boko Haram members around the Musiri and Ndufu villages, Ngala LGA (Borno). An unspecified number of ISWAP/Boko Haram members were killed and various camps were destroyed; 30 abductees were rescued. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals intercepted and abducted six travelers from a commercial bus at Ochaja (Dekina, Kogi). The abductees include (presumed not armed) NYSC members and a pregnant woman; the abductees were rescued and the abductors were arrested by Amotekun Corps, there are no reports of a clash.
On 19 March 2022, two Naval officers stabbed and shot a medical doctor in Lekki (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos) after a disagreement over a parking lot. The victim was wounded, and taken to the hospital.

On 19 March 2022, Ndaka and Ichen ethnic militias clashed in Bissaula (Kurmi, Taraba). Three policemen and one woman were killed as the policemen were deployed to the location and overpowered by one of the groups; properties were also destroyed.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals tied up and beat the gatekeeper of a politician's house in in Ondo (Ondo West, Ondo). The house was vandalized and set ablaze; there were no occupants of in the building during the attack, believed to be politically related. The politician family had suffered other attacks previously.

On 19 March 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons on their way to Idoani (Ose, Ondo). The abductees were a cocoa farmer, and a female and a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded, they escaped from the bush after their abductors fell asleep at night.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals on 10 motorcycles attacked members of Abba Vigilance Group and Abba Security Network in Nkwangele LGA (Imo), coded as Abba. The assailants, who attacked from Okwelle community, shot at the defense militiamen who fled, leaving their patrol van that was set ablaze by the assailants. There were no casualties.

On 19 March 2022, ISWAP militants clashed with the military as they attacked a military base and were repelled by soldiers in Doron Baga (Kukawa, Borno). Scores of militants were killed, several others were wounded. The group was armed with grenades and five gun trucks. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals abducted a university teacher, his wife and four others near Ewatto (Esan South East, Edo). The wife was released on the same day and asked to mobilize for ransom by the abductors, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.
On 19 March 2022, unidentified armed individuals attacked a police station and killed two policemen at Umuoguma (Owerri West, Imo). Police sources claim that the attack was repelled.

On 19 March 2022, armed individuals attacked a member of the PDP in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The victim was beaten, shot in the leg by the assailants and was later rescued and taken to the hospital; the reason for the attack is presumed to be political.

On 20 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists in large numbers attacked civilians and killed around 34 persons in Mararaban, Adan, Tsonje, Katanga, Kadarko, all in Kagoro chiefdom, Kaura LGA (Kaduna) [coded to Kagoro] and Agban (coded separately). Over 200 houses and 32 shops were set on fire, 17 motorcycles were vandalized. The attack would be a reprisal to the killing of one pastoralist on the previous week [coded separately]. Fatalities split into 2 events, coded as 17.

On 20 March 2022, Nigerian soldiers repelled an attack by Sokoto militiamen on traders along Sokoto-Goronyo road (Goronyo, Sokoto). The militiamen blocked the road with the intention of robbing and abducting traders; casualties unknown.
On 20 March 2022, a policeman killed a scrap collector in Agbor (Ika South, Delta) following the victim's refusal to pay a bribe of 1000 naira.

On 20 March 2022, a Zamfara militia killed between 16 to 20 civilians, including the village head, of Ganar-Kiywa (Bukkuyum, Zamfara), coded to Bukuyum. 62 persons were also abducted from the areas and Bungudu LGA [coded separately].

On 20 March 2022, an unidentified armed group of four abducted a man from Ozoro town (Isoko North, Delta). The abductee was rescued by policemen after the abductors abandoned him and fled because the policemen were on their trail.

On 20 March 2022, a local defense militia clash with an armed group presumably around Araromi-Opin (Ekiti, Kwara) while trying to rescue persons abducted on 16 March by the group (coded separately). One female abductee, who was a women leader of the APC, was killed during the clash; an unspecified number of the defense militia members were wounded, one in critical condition.

On 20 March 2022, suspected Fulani pastoralists killed two military officers in Agban (Kaura, Kaduna) as the group attacked the village and Adan, Tsonje, Katanga, Kadarko, all in Kagoro chiefdom, Kaura LGA [coded separately]. Around 34 people were killed, over 200 houses and 32 shops were set on fire, 17 motorcycles were vandalized. The attack would be a reprisal to the killing of one pastoralist on the previous week [coded separately]. Fatalities split into 2 events, coded as 17.

On 20 March 2022, suspected IPOB militants in large numbers attacked a police divisional headquarters and clashed with policemen and DSS operatives in Omuma (Oru East, Imo). Four militants were killed, others fled and a number of them were wounded. Five different undetonated IEDs were recovered.

On 21 March 2022, Zamfara militiamen abducted one 60 year old woman from Gambanda (Gummi, Zamfara). The victim was rescued by the police, her abductors were arrested. There are no reports about a clash during the rescue.

On 21 March 2022, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians in Tadurga, Tungar Danyaki, Tungar Samari, Tungar Mele, Tungar Danyaki in Kebu ward (Danko, Kebbi). A local defense militia chairman (presumed unharmed) and 12 others civilians were killed in Tungar Danyaki, while many houses shops and canteens were burnt in Tungar Gongo. The attacks were carried out for three days (between 21 to 23 March). 13 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 5.

On 21 March 2022, armed individuals abducted two pastoralists (assumed Fulani), rustled 400 cattle, burnt down houses and food items when they invaded Pinau (Wase, Plateau). There are no reports about demands for ransom.
Around 21 March 2022 (as reported), a Zamfara militia killed 17 civilians in Juyi and Doruwa, Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). 62 persons were also abducted from the areas and Bukkuyum [coded separately].

On 22 March 2022, for the second day, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians in Tadurga, Tungar Danyaki, Kebu, Tungar Samari, Tungar Mele, Tungar Danyaki and Kebu in Kebu ward (Danko, Kebbi). A local defense militia chairman (presumed unharmed) and 12 others civilians were killed in Tungar Danyaki, while many houses shops and canteens were burnt in Tungar Gongo. The attacks were carried out for three days (between 21 to 23 March). 13 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 22 March 2022, armed individuals attacked two traditional rulers of Yola community, killing one, in Yola (Wase, Plateau). The motorcycle the victims were travelling in was stolen, other sources report the assailants to be suspected armed robbers.
On 22 March 2022, a Fulani militia, working together with a members of a group linked to Terwase Akwaza, attacked civilians around Ankya, Mbamena (Ukum, Benue). Three persons were killed.

On 22 March 2022, Niger militiamen attacked and killed a farmer, who was also a local gun fabricator, in Shashai, Kuchi ward (Muya, Niger). One other individual was shot and wounded; two men, seven women and their children were also abducted. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 22 March 2022, a Katsina militia attacked and killed at least two people in Mai Bakko village, Sabuwa LGA (Katsina), coded to Sabuwa. An unspecified number of persons were abducted.

On 22 March 2022, armed individuals abducted three persons from Godozhi community (Kuje, FCT). One of the abductors is a pastor of the ECWA church, the other two are sons of the former LEA secretary in Kuje area council. The abductees were released on 25 March after an undisclosed amount, foodstuff, drugs and drinks were paid as ransom.

On 22 March 2022, armed individuals invaded a pastoralists' settlement (assumed Fulani) and abducted three persons in Achido in Abaji LGA (FCT), coded to Abaji. A ransom of 6 million naira, two bags of rice and wine has been demanded.

On 22 March 2022, Katsina militiamen numbering up to 300 attacked a checkpoint with mobile policemen along the Kankara-Sheme road (Kankara, Katsina). An unspecified number of policemen were killed, some residents were reported killed by stray bullets. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 22 March 2022, the Police repelled Fulani pastoralists during an attack on Mararabar-Kankara community, Kankara LGA (Katsina), coded to Kankara. The residents claimed that at least five communities, Gidan Dankunda, Kungiya, Gidan Kurty, Centan Dangera and Gidan Malumfashi were attacked after residents recovered cattle from the group; at least 5 non-pastoralists were killed.

On 23 March 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed an unspecified number of civilians in Moon ward (Kwande, Benue), and Mbadula and Mbakyior wards (coded separately). Several houses were burnt down; unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 23 March 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed an unspecified number of civilians in Mbadula and Mbakyior wards in Kwande LGA (Benue) [coded to Adikpom], and Moon (coded separately). Several houses were burnt; unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 23 March 2022, armed pastoralists (assumed Fulani) attacked a farmer in his farm, beat him and killed him at Wuyan Yobe in Guri LGA (Jigawa). The crops on the farm were destroyed by the assailants.
Around 23 March 2022 (week of), an unidentified cult militia killed a member of another cult militia in Kabawa, Lokoja LGA (Kogi).

On 23 March 2022, for the third day, Zamfara militiamen attacked civilians in Tadurga, Tungar Danyaki, Kebu, Tungar Samari, Tungar Mele, Tungar Danyaki and Kebu in Kebu ward (Danko, Kebbi). A local defense militia chairman (presumed unharmed) and 12 others civilians were killed in Tungar Danyaki, while many houses shops and canteens were burnt in Tungar Gongo. The attacks were carried out for three days (between 21 to 23 March). 13 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 23 March 2022, armed individuals killed a cattle merchant, abducted his wife and two sons from their residence in Garin Mallam Audu (Yorro, Taraba). The victim and his family were abducted and led to an undisclosed location before he was shot; there are no reports about ransom demands yet.
On 23 March 2022, members of a Sokoto militia attacked and killed two civilians in Kwargaba (Wurno, Sokoto). The assailants also looted shops and rustled cattle.

On 23 March 2022, armed individuals attacked and killed a presumed off duty Ebube Agu Corps member at his residence in Ezza North LGA (Ebonyi), coded to Ebiaji. The victim was the commander of Ebubu Agu in the local government area; the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 23 March 2022, members of a Sokoto militia shot and killed four farmers at their farm in Gatawa district (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). The victims were killed for refusing the assailants' cattle to graze on their farm.
On 23 March 2022, members of a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Masu, Bungudu LGA (Zamfara), killed one and wounded another person. 30 others, including women and children were abducted.

Around 24 March 2022 (as reported), soldiers tortured and killed a man at Ibodi (Atakumosa West, Osun) following a misunderstanding between the victim and some soldiers dressed in plain clothes. The victims friends were also arrested by the soldiers.

On 24 March 2022, suspected members of Aiye/ Black axe cult militia killed a suspected member of Eiye confraternity at Oluwo (Abeokuta North, Ogun). The victim's body suggested he was killed with an axe or machete; the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 24 March 2022, military forces during a clearance operation destroyed Boko Haram/ISWAP camps around Ukuba and Camp Zairo in Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). Several militants were killed, others fled, weapons and equipment were recovered according the Nigerian Defence headquarters. Several fatalities coded as 3.

On 24 March 2022, armed individuals numbering over 20 abducted one woman and two men from Chukuku community (Kuje, FCT). The abductors shoot sporadically during the raid, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 25 March 2022, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted two men at Owa-Oyibu (Ika North East, Delta). A ransom of 13 million naira has been demanded.

On 25 March 2022, members of Black Axe cult militia, also called Aiye, killed an Eiye Cult member in a reprisal attack at Seme Border (Badagry, Lagos). The victim, who was a student, was macheted severally before he was shot at close range.

On 25 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked and killed about 50 civilians in Tama, Gidan Alhaji Kida, Kadanya, Durumi, Giwa LGA (Kaduna), Dillalai, Kaya, Barebari and Ungwan Dan Bako [coded separately]. An unspecified number of people were abducted and over 100 cows seized. Of the 50, 15 were killed in Dallalai; 35 fatalities split in 4 events, coded as 9

On 25 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked and killed about 50 civilians in Barebari (Giwa, Kaduna), Tama, Gidan Alhaji Kida, Kadanya, Durumi, Dillalai, Kaya, Kaya and Ungwan Dan Bako [coded separately]. An unspecified number of people were abducted and over 100 cows seized. Of the 50, 15 were killed in Dallalai; 35 fatalities split in 4 events, coded as 9.

On 25 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia killed about 50 civilians in 9 communities, including, Dillalai (Giwa, Kaduna), Zango Tama, Kaya, Barebari, Ungwan Dan Bako, Gidan Alhaji Kida, Kadanya and Durumi [coded separately]. An unspecified number of people were abducted and over 100 cows seized. 15 people were killed in Dillalai, five commercial trucks and five houses were burnt.

On 25 March 2022, armed individuals abducted the son of the Minister of Communication and Digital Economy in Bauchi state. The victim was found at a checkpoint in Dambam LGA (Bauchi), there are no reports about ransom payment.

On 25 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked and killed about 50 civilians in Ungwan Dan Bako (Giwa, Kaduna), Tama, Gidan Alhaji Kida, Kadanya, Durumi, Dillalai, Kaya, Kaya and Berebari [coded separately]. An unspecified number of people were abducted and over 100 cows seized. Of the 50, 15 were killed in Dallalai; 35 fatalities split in 4 events, coded as 8.
On 25 March 2022, a policeman stabbed and killed two civilians in Yelwa (Bauchi, Bauchi). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 25 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked and killed about 50 civilians in Kaya (Giwa, Kaduna), Tama, Gidan Alhaji Kida, Kadanya, Durumi, Dillalai, Kaya, Barebari and Ungwan Dan Bako [coded separately]. An unspecified number of people were abducted and over 100 cows seized. Of the 50, 15 were killed in Dallalai; 35 fatalities split in 4 events, coded as 9.

On 25 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen clashed with soldiers around the airport in Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna) around midnight, claiming that the soldiers were taking away their cattle. Several rustled cows were recovered.

Around 26 March 2022 (as reported), a militia operating from the Cameroon border killed an unidentified number of Ichen individuals in Bissaula (Kurmi, Taraba). The group would be working for a party in the Ndaka/Ichen ethnic crisis. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 26 March 2022, members of a Niger militia killed one person by setting him ablaze in Zagzaga (Muya, Niger). Many houses were set ablaze, shops and houses were looted by the assailants who attacked various communities until the following day [coded separately].

On 26 March 2022, members of a Niger militia attacked residents of Chibiani (Muya, Niger), killing at least one man and abducting 30 people. This was the first attack of a series in different communities and in the LGA and Paikoro LGA that lasted till the following day [coded separately].

On 26 March 2022, members of a Niger militia attacked residents of Mutun Daya, Njita, Tshon Kabula and Jesso (Muya, Niger) and Chibiani (coded separately). No fewer than 10 people were killed. Fatalities coded as 9 (1 in Chibiani).

Around 26 March 2022 (between 24 - 28 March), Kaduna militiamen attacked and killed at least 52 civilians in Giwa LGA (Kaduna) and Birin Gwari LGA [coded separately]. 130 others were abducted, 10,463 persons were displaced. 52 fatalities split across two events coded as 26.

Around 26 March 2022 (between 24 - 28 March), Kaduna militiamen attacked and killed at least 52 civilians in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna) and Giwa LGA [coded separately]. 130 others were abducted, 10,463 persons were displaced. 52 fatalities split across two events coded as 26.

On 26 March 2022, policemen clashed with an armed group related to the Gana group at New City, Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). Four militiamen were killed, the others fled. The assailants were enroute to attack Gbagire village when they were intercepted by the policemen.

On 26 March 2022, suspected Icelanders militia, clashed with Bobos cult militia members in Swali (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). One Bobos member was killed; the victim was macheted and burnt, other sources report that the victim was killed by a mob after he was caught during an armed robbery.

On 26 March 2022, Kaduna militiamen, numbering over 200, clashed with soldiers on the airport in Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna) as the group invaded the airport, killed one Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA) staff and prevented a flight from taking off . Military sources stated 12 militiamen were killed in an airstrike during the encounter and that the airport was not attacked, rather the militiamen were only taking the back route through the airport. The event happened after militiamen clashed with the military and rustled cows around the airport during the night [coded separately]. Fatalities coded as 13.

Around 26 March 2022 (as reported), policemen engaged Zamfara militiamen in an armed clash after the militiamen were sighted heading towards Koran Ganawa (Tsafe, Zamfara). One militiaman was killed, two rifles and one motorcycle were recovered.
On 26 March 2022, Kutep and Jukun ethnic militias clashed at Takum (Takum, Taraba). Several people were killed, coded as 3.

On 26 March 2022, Kutep ethnic militia clashed with security agents, presumed police, at Takum (Takum, Taraba), after security forces stopped a Kutep procession. Three Kutep were killed by security agents. A curfew was imposed on the town. Later, fighting broke out with a Jukun militia (coded separately).
On 27 March 2022, a member of the Civilian JTF shot and wounded a driver in Gubio LGA (Borno) following the victim's attempt to settle a conflict between the CJTF member and another driver.

On 27 March 2022, Niger militiamen abducted 45 villagers, including a Catholic priest, looted shops and displaced people when they invaded at least six communities along the Sarkin Pawa- Gwada road (Muya, Niger). A series of attacks in the region started on the previous day in Muya LGA and continued until the following night in several communities of the Muya and Paikoro LGAs (coded separately). The priest was released on 8 April after an undisclosed amount was paid.
On 27 March 2022, members of a Kaduna militia attacked residents of Hayin Kanwa (Giwa, Kaduna). At least 15 persons were killed.

On 27 March 2022, Eiye Cult militiamen and members of Aiye also called Black Axe militia clashed in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) in a supremacy battle. At least 7 persons were killed in different areas of the metropolis.
On 27 March 2022, an armed group shot and killed one person in Aguluzigbo (Aniocha, Anambra), coded to Agulu. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 28 March 2022, two unidentified cult militias clashed in in the Kabawa area, in or around Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi) in reprisal of killing of the a member of one of the groups the previous week (coded separately). The police confirmed one person was killed, while others stated at least 4 fatalities. Houses belonging to assumed rival militias were burned.

On 28 March 2022, Black Axe cult militiamen clashed with Eiye confraternity members in different areas of Shagamu city (Shagamu, Ogun), including, Ajegunle, Soyindo, Ijagba, and Sabo. At least eight persons were killed, residents fled the area.

On 28 March 2022, soldiers clashed with IPOB/ESN militants during a clearance operation at one of their camps in Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). 41 guns and 6 cutlasses were recovered after the group fled. There were no casualties.

On 28 March 2022, a Kaduna militia clashed with soldiers after the militia derailed a train carrying between 350 to 900 civilians with explosives and shot at the passengers at Dutse (Chikun, Kaduna). Between 8 and 9 civilians were killed in the attack, 22 to 41 others were wounded and at least 68 were abducted. The NRC claims 14 out of the 21 missing passengers were found alive, and some abducted victims were released after a payment of a ransom. The attack was initially claimed by Ansaru who released a statement on 2 June denying their involvement in the attack. 11 abductees were released on 11 June in return for the release of the children of the assailants, 7 abductees were released around 9 July, 3 others were released on 24 July, another 5 were released around 1 August and 7 others were released on 10 August. Four victims were released on 19 August, the remaining 23 abductees were released on 4 October, the government claimed that no ransom was paid.

On 28 March 2022, armed individuals killed three women in Mararaban Tipper, near Nzhwerenvi village, and killed one man and injured three others along the Gero road around the Tin Mining Site, all in Bassa LGA (Plateau), coded to nearby Kpara.
On 28 March 2022, Icelanders and Greenlanders clashed in Itu LGA (Akwa Ibom) over unspecified reasons. 15 people were killed and many others were wounded.

On 28 March 2022, an armed group shot and killed a commercial bus driver, abducted 18 passengers, including a former chairman of the NUJ, around the Evwreni community (Ughelli North, Delta). A ransom of 5 million naira has been demanded for the release of the former NUJ chairman. The police claim about 7 persons were abducted. The journalist was released around 2 April; there are no details about ransom payment.

Around 28 March 2022 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a journalist and some other civilians on the Evwreni road, coded to Evwreni (Ughelli North, Delta). The group were on their way to Warri from Yenaga. Police officers were able to rescue the abducted.
